children: OTTAWA, Sept 3 (Reuters) - Canada's trade surplus narrowed to C$769 million ($557 million) in July, as exports fell and imports grew, Statistics Canada said on Thursday. This was the fifth consecutive monthly surplus.    Exports fell by 2.3%, on metal and non-metallic mineral products, as well as energy products. Imports grew by 2.2%, on motor vehicles and parts, as well as metal and non-metallic mineral products.    Following are the seasonally adjusted figures in billions of Canadian dollars:

Merchandise trade     Jul  Jun (rev) change pct  Jun (prev)   Balance             +0.769    +4.201       n/a       +3.856Exports             76.137    77.959      -2.3       77.486Imports             75.368    73.758      +2.2       73.631
NOTE: Analysts surveyed by Reuters had forecast a trade surplus of C$3.57 billion in July.  ($1=$1.3804 Canadian)  (Reporting by Dale Smith; editing by Promit Mukherjee) ((promit.mukherjee@tr.com))
